title: Security material and TLS authority
summary: Addresses carry a security-profile reference, not certificates, trust stores or private keys. The QUIC provider resolves that profile and OpenSSL owns TLS 1.3 and QUIC cryptographic protocol mechanics.
invariants: Never embed private key, certificate or trust-store bytes in QuicSocketAddress.
Security profile resolution is provider-side authority.
Peer verification and SNI/ALPN configuration remain explicit provider configuration.
A successful QUIC handshake is transport security evidence; it does not authorize application actions.
